In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the number of VNFs in a chain is a more critical factor in determining bandwidth consumption compared to the number of VFN replicas and NFV nodes.
SC mapping with multiple instances of a SC can be done with a small set of instances and the number of VNFs in the SC does not have much of an effect on bandwidth consumption.
, for a given number of NFV servers, a small number of VNFs is sufficient for the deployment of a large number of SC instances.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, with a small number of SC instances and a small number of VNFs, one can deploy a service chain over a wide-area network with a minimum bandwidth consumption.
, for the first time, we have proposed and solved the problem of SC deployment with multiple instances in a WAN.

, for the first time, we show how to deploy multiple SC instances to serve traffic flows in a WAN, and how this approach can help us to analyze the impact of VNF replication and NFV node distribution on bandwidth consumption.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for large networks, the number of SC instances required for minimum bandwidth consumption is small.
, in order to minimize bandwidth consumption, it might be better to deploy a small number of VNF instances instead of a single large instance.
